B1.instr:
Answer all 20 questions. Each question has exactly one correct option and is worth one mark. No marks are deducted for wrong answers. Unless a question says otherwise, all angles are in radians and all logarithms may be taken to any fixed base. Record your answers as letters on the grid below before consulting the solutions. 

\textbf{Difficulty note.} This paper contains no routine questions. Every item is pitched at the level of the final third of a real TMUA paper, and most rely on a method or trap that a standard school course does not teach. Finishing in 75 minutes is meant to be difficult, so score by what you get right, not by what you finish.

B2.instr:
Answer all 20 questions. Each question has exactly one correct option and is worth one mark. No marks are deducted for wrong answers. Unless a question says otherwise, all angles are in radians. Throughout, ``must be true'' means true in every case allowed by the given information, and ``can be true'' means true in at least one such case. Record your answers as letters on the grid below before consulting the solutions. 

\textbf{Difficulty note.} This paper tests reasoning rather than technique, at a level above the standard TMUA. The ideas are the ones a first olympiad course teaches: find the quantity that does not change, count something two ways, look at remainders, find the losing positions. None of the questions is a known problem with a known answer; each is a fresh instance, and each has at least one option that a plausible half-argument makes look correct.

C1.instr: Answer all 20 questions. Each question has exactly one correct option and is worth one mark. No marks are deducted for wrong answers. All angles are in radians. This set is pitched well above the 2025 TMUA and weighted towards integration tricks and trigonometric inequalities. Nothing beyond the TMUA specification is needed, but almost nothing yields to a routine method.

C2.instr: Answer all 20 questions. Each question has exactly one correct option and is worth one mark. No marks are deducted for wrong answers. All angles are in radians. This set is weighted towards implications and their negations, redundant and independent conditions, and reasoning with trigonometric inequalities and integrals.

D1.instr: Answer all 20 questions. Each question has exactly one correct option and is worth one mark. No marks are deducted for wrong answers. Every question uses AS content only. The difficulty lies in how that content is used: parameters that change the case, conditions that quietly remove a solution, and answers that come from structure rather than from brute force.
